tools.name: describe_business
tools.description: What Commonstop does, what happens to a request, and the request fields.

tools.name: submit_request
tools.description: Send a requirement to Commonstop. It is kept with a reference number. Your request is recorded and you receive a reference number. Commonstop reviews the prepared requirement and open questions, confirms scope and coverage, seeks provider pricing and terms, and replies by email to the address you le

tools.name: request_status
tools.description: Resume a requirement using the receipt credentials. Read the recorded requirement and any linked offers. Contact details are kept apart.

tools.name: inspect_offer
tools.description: Read the exact authorized terms, terms hash, order state and processor payment links. Use the offer link credentials, or credentials of the request explicitly linked to this offer.

tools.name: accept_offer
tools.description: Place an order on terms you have inspected and the buyer has authorized you to accept. Requires the exact terms hash and explicit acceptance. Follow inspect_offer later for payment links and verified payment state.

tools.name: decline_offer
tools.description: Decline an issued offer on its inspected terms.

tools.name: release_payment
tools.description: Confirm a payment condition only where the inspected order allows the customer to release it. This records approval; it does not pay the processor.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_request · Private data: submit_request, request_status, inspect_offer, release_payment · Public sink: submit_request · Destructive: submit_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_request · Private data: submit_request, request_status, inspect_offer, release_payment · Public sink: submit_request · Destructive: submit_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
